evidence_quotes.quid_pro_quo: Rep says 'this will just take about ten minutes. Sounds good' but does not deliver the full framing about a dependable quote or wait for a clear yes — moves into email collection immediately.
evidence_quotes.their_agenda: Rep asks: 'what are your biggest concerns for your upcoming move. You know, what are your most important things you want answers to on this call today?' Asked before probing starts.
evidence_quotes.two_layers_deep: Customer states only concern is 'price, a quote just the price of, of how much it would be.' No follow-up probing ('tell me more about that') — rep pivots to logistics. N/A applied because the customer raised no substantive concern beyond price.
evidence_quotes.active_listening_reflection: No reflection summary attempted. N/A applied because customer raised no layered concerns to reflect back.
evidence_quotes.logistics_details_gathered: Property type (house), stories (one story), rooms (one bedroom), walking distance (ten feet), special items (hutch with antiques), fragile/valuable items (hutch antique), large furniture (bed, frame, dressers, mirror, hutch), boxes (15 range), access concerns (asked). All seven logistics items covered.
evidence_quotes.box_count_asked: Rep asks: 'how about for the boxes a typical one bedroom usually has fifteen to 25 do you feel like you will fall within that range?' Yes, asked and confirmed at lower range.
evidence_quotes.estimate_anchor: Rep provides: 'a typical one bedroom worth of items typically has like, you know, it will take like two mover with two movers, one truck between two and a half to three and a half hours to completely move. So, in your case, since you are moving from a one story house to an apartment in Midland, Texas... I would estimate your move to be at nine hours.' Personalized by noting one-story house, apartment destination, unknown floor, and 5.5-hour drive. Full anchor and personalization present.
evidence_quotes.pricing_framing: Rep discloses: trip fee $2,160, hourly rate $200/two movers, 26-foot box truck, no hidden fees (no credit card fees, no stair fees, no disassembly fees), 2.5-hour minimum, 15-minute increments. Both transparency and commitment framing present.
evidence_quotes.feels_fair_then_silence: Rep does not ask 'Does that feel fair?' or any version. After laying out the pricing and nine-hour estimate with $3,960 total, rep asks only 'do you have questions or clarifications about that?' and customer responds 'Nope, I have no question.' No version of feels-fair ask detected.
evidence_quotes.on_time_guarantee_delivered: Rep states: 'we have the on time guarantee. So we value your time if we could make it in the time window that we arrange. We immediately start discounting money of your final bill.' Discount terms covered. Full delivery.
evidence_quotes.damage_coverage_delivered: Rep says: 'we have the no worries damage coverage. So, well, our free evaluation coverage included in our hourly rate and we provide up to $2,000 per move to repair, replace or reimburse for accidental damages.' Covers $2,000 and that it's included (built-in), but does not explicitly state 'no deductible' or 'no fine print' framing. Partial delivery.
evidence_quotes.closes_the_loop: Rep does not ask a version of 'Does that put those to rest?' or confirm the two promises settled the customer's concerns. No close-the-loop ask.
evidence_quotes.final_concerns_check: Rep does not ask 'What's still concerning you about this move?' or any genuine final concerns version. Call moves directly to the ask without a genuine final check.
evidence_quotes.catch_all_asked: Rep does not ask 'Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?' No catch-all.
evidence_quotes.explicit_ask: Rep asks: 'would you like our help with your, with your move on October 2nd?' This is plainly asked but the customer's objection ('I'm gonna keep looking around, I think that maybe I just don't have enough stuff to need a full moving company...') is met with acceptance. The rep does not re-pitch or close, treating the soft no as final. The ask itself is plain (no built-in out offered by rep), so 'full' on form, but no actual booking attempt follows.
evidence_quotes.rate_lock_mentioned: Rep does not mention rate-lock or no-deposit terms.
evidence_quotes.booking_confirmed: No booking details confirmed. Customer declines to book and rep only confirms email follow-up: 'I'll be sending you an email with the code with a game plan and the pricing, so that if you decide to book with us, you have a reference with you and you can just give us a call back to confirm the schedule.' No date, phone, arrival window, crew size, addresses, or crew notes confirmed because no booking was made.

top_strength: Jevic gathered comprehensive logistics details (property type, stories, rooms, walking distance, special items, furniture inventory, box count, access) and delivered a well-anchored, personalized estimate that accounted for the long-distance drive and the customer's specific situation.
coaching_note: Skip the 'any questions?' close and instead ask 'Does that feel fair?' with real silence, then run a genuine final concerns check ('What's still concerning you?') and a catch-all ('Anything coming with you we haven't talked about?') before the ask — these three moves together often recover soft objections and create real booking opportunities.
